- If sentiment is consistently neutral (0.00) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- When model shows sharp upward spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), true outcome often lags or overshoots — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days of downward trend), model tends to overcorrect upward — adjust forecast to align with recent mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply slight downward adjustment for days 1–5.
- If sentiment history includes a single non-zero value (e.g., 0.25), model may overreact — reduce forecast magnitude by 3–5% relative to baseline.
- Model frequently underestimates true price when recent history is volatile — increase forecast by 2–4% for volatile periods.
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome across multiple examples, apply a global downward shift of 1–3% for all forecasts unless sentiment indicates bullish momentum.
